messages:
alex: Heads-up — we had a p99 tail-latency spike on prod serving pool-7, ~10:03-10:13 UTC. SLO alerts kicked. Looks correlated with a batch of long prompts + a burst of tool-calls. Can someone pick this up?

maya: I grabbed the request traces. Most requests that spiked had prompt lengths > 4k tokens and a handful invoked external tool plugins repeatedly (3-7 calls).

priya: Any kernel-selection mismatches in the logs? We recently landed the new seq-length heuristic in the runtime. Could be misrouting long contexts to a suboptimal kernel.

alex: Good question. I pulled the request metadata and kernel decisions. For several long contexts the runtime chose the "fast-32b-tiling" kernel (optimized for 2k-3k typical), not the "longstream-kv-friendly" kernel. That caused repeated KV repacking and slowed the KV cache warm path.

perf-bot: Automated profile snapshot attached for the window 10:04-10:06. Top stacks (samples):
```
24.1% runtime::kv_cache_eviction_lock
18.7% runtime::kernel_selector::evaluate(heuristic)
15.6% runtime::kernel_execute_fast32b
12.3% rpc::toolcall::wait
8.9% memcpy
6.4% kernel_fallback_cpu_path
```

Note: elevated syscall times on nodes 7 and 9.

maya: The profile shows contention around kv cache eviction lock. Tool-calls are interleaving and causing repeated cache invalidation because we don't pin tool-generated tokens to the same KV shard. Also kernel selection is thrashing due to quick changes in observed sequence length during prefix processing.

tom: Reproducer idea: feed a long prompt with intermittent tool calls that inject short generated sequences, e.g., pattern: [4k prompt] -> generate 200 tokens -> tool call -> generate 50 tokens -> tool call -> generate 500 tokens. That toggles the heuristic between long-optimized and short-optimized kernels on the same session.

priya: Yep. Two immediate hypotheses: (1) heuristic mispredicts because it uses last-n tokens distribution which is clipped when tool calls return short tokens, (2) KV cache eviction policy is too eager on microbatch concurrency spike, causing lock contention.

alex: Quick mitigation proposal: 1) short-term: add a sticky kernel binding per session for X seconds (disable per-chunk re-eval), 2) reduce eviction aggressiveness when tool-call flags are present, 3) increase microbatch max size for this pool to reduce incoming concurrency. Thoughts?

maya: Sticky binding seems low-risk and should drop kernel-selector churn immediately. We can roll as an operator config flag targeting pool-7.

priya: I'll prototype sticky binding toggle and a TTL of 30s. Also will change KV eviction to prefer LRU-with-pin for tool sessions.

tom: I simulated the reproducer locally — with sticky binding p99 dropped from ~1.5s to ~320ms on my microbench. Without sticky binding, the kernel selector sampling cost alone adds ~120-180ms per generate chunk in our test.

perf-bot: Note from infra-bot: nodes 7 and 9 had a concurrent GC on the same epoch earlier which may have amplified syscall pauses. Noted in system logs: "gc: compaction pause 210ms" at 10:05:12 on node-9.

alex: Okay plan: Priya implements sticky binding + KV pin change behind feature flag. Maya will patch operator to flip flag for pool-7. Tom to run scaled repro (50 concurrent sessions) and push metrics. I'll prepare a rollback plan.

maya: Will do. Targeting canary rollout in 30m.

alex: Thanks everyone. Leave notes here when canary results look stable. :thumbsup:

priya: created PR draft with sticky kernel toggle and KV pin heuristics, link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4823 (WIP) :eyes:

tom: Ran scaled sim, canary reduces p99 over 10m window from 1.2s -> 410ms. No increased error rate. Logs show fewer kernel_switch events.

maya: Canary looks good on pool-7 after 45m. Rolling to remaining pools incrementally.

alex: Follow-up actions: 1) instrument kernel_selector re-eval count per-session, 2) add alert if kv_cache_eviction_lock contends > 5% sample rate, 3) add a unit test for tool-call friendly pinning behavior. I'll add these to the backlog.

priya: Added tickets and bumped priority. Closing this thread once rollout is fully done.

infra-bot: Deploy to pool-7 flagged as SUCCESS at 11:23:10 UTC.

maya: Closing loop — observed sustained p99 reduction and steady throughput. Leaving monitoring on for 24h. :white_check_mark:
